lessons.title: Recap: Signs of Spring
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe multiple signs that spring has arrived.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap signs of spring from Week 23.
lessons.main_activity: Go on a spring walk or look at pictures, recording signs of spring seen (flowers, buds, baby animals, longer days).
key_questions: What signs of spring can you see?
How is spring different from winter?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note deepened seasonal observation skill — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Look for more signs of spring on a walk together.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'Jasper's Beanstalk' by Nick Butterworth
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe what Jasper did to help his bean grow.
lessons.main_activity: Read the story, discussing how Jasper cared for his bean and what he learned about patience.
key_questions: What did Jasper do to help the bean grow?
What did he learn?

differentiation.extension: Explain the story's message about patience

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension and understanding of a moral/message — evidence for LIT.1.
lessons.plenary: Discuss the importance of patience when growing plants.
lessons.home_link: Talk about something you had to be patient for.

lessons.title: Counting Seeds
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count seeds accurately up to 10.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at and count a handful of seeds together.
lessons.main_activity: Children count out a given number of seeds to plant, checking accuracy.
key_questions: How many seeds do you have?
Can you count them again to check?

differentiation.extension: Count to 10+ and compare with a partner

lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting accuracy — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.home_link: Count small objects (seeds, buttons) at home together.

lessons.title: Decorating a Plant Pot
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to decorate a plant pot using pattern and colour.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at examples of decorated plant pots.
lessons.main_activity: Children decorate a small plant pot (or paper wrap for one) using paint and pattern, ready for planting.
resources_needed: Small pots or paper wraps, paint, craft materials
key_questions: What pattern are you using?
What colours have you chosen?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe pattern-making and fine motor control — evidence for EAD.1/MATHS.2.
lessons.home_link: Decorate a pot or container together at home.

lessons.title: Planting Seeds
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to plant a seed correctly, describing the steps taken.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap what plants need to grow (Week 5).
lessons.main_activity: Children plant a seed in their decorated pot from Monday, following the steps (soil, seed, cover, water) with adult guidance.
resources_needed: Pots from Monday, soil, seeds, watering can
key_questions: What did you do first?
What does your seed need now?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note practical skill and understanding of planting process — evidence for UTW.3/PD.2.
lessons.plenary: Set up a watering rota for the planted seeds.
lessons.home_link: Plant a seed together at home if possible.

lessons.title: Writing a Plant Diary Entry
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write about their planting experience.
lessons.main_activity: Children draw their planted seed and attempt to write a simple sentence (e.g. 'I planted a seed') using known phonics sounds.
key_questions: What did you plant?
Can you write about it?

differentiation.extension: Independent phonetic attempt at a short sentence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note writing progress and purposeful recording — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Share plant diary entries with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Start a simple plant diary together if growing something at home.

lessons.title: Measuring Plant Growth (Prediction)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to predict and later measure how tall a plant might grow.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how plants grow taller over time.
lessons.main_activity: Children predict how tall they think their seed will grow using non-standard units (cubes), to be checked later in the term.
key_questions: How tall do you think it will grow?
How will we measure it?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note early measurement and prediction skill — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.home_link: Predict how tall a plant at home might grow.

lessons.title: Parts of a Plant
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name the main parts of a plant (root, stem, leaf, flower).
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a real plant and point out visible parts.
lessons.main_activity: Label a large plant diagram with root, stem, leaf, and flower, discussing what each part does.
resources_needed: Real plant or large diagram, labels
key_questions: What is this part called?
What does the root do?

differentiation.extension: Label all 4 parts and explain their function

lessons.assessment_notes: Note plant part vocabulary and function understanding — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap the parts of a plant.
lessons.home_link: Look at a plant at home and name its parts.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'The Tiny Seed' by Eric Carle
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe the journey of the tiny seed.
lessons.main_activity: Read 'The Tiny Seed', discussing the seed's journey and what happens to it through the seasons.
key_questions: What happens to the seed on its journey?
Why does it survive when others don't?

differentiation.extension: Explain reasoning for the seed's survival

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension and reasoning — evidence for LIT.1.
lessons.plenary: Discuss the story's journey through the seasons.
lessons.home_link: Talk about how seeds travel (wind, birds, animals) with family.

lessons.title: Symmetry in Flowers
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify symmetry in flower shapes.
lessons.main_activity: Children fold paper flower shapes in half to check for symmetry, then create their own symmetrical flower design.
key_questions: Is this flower symmetrical?
How do you know?

differentiation.extension: Create own symmetrical flower design independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note symmetry understanding — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.home_link: Look for symmetrical flowers or petals outside.

lessons.title: Checking on Our Planted Seeds
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to observe and describe any changes in their planted seed.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap what was planted on Tuesday.
lessons.main_activity: Children observe and record (drawing) any changes in their planted seeds, discussing what's happening.
resources_needed: Planted pots from Tuesday, observation sheet
key_questions: What has changed?
What do you think will happen next?

differentiation.support: Adult prompts what to look for

lessons.assessment_notes: Note observational and scientific language — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Check on any plants growing at home.

lessons.title: Retelling 'The Tiny Seed'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retell the story's key events in sequence.
lessons.main_activity: Using picture cards, children retell the story sequence using sequencing words.
key_questions: What happened first?
What happened at the end?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note sequencing and retelling ability — evidence for LIT.1/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: One group retells to the class.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story to someone at home.

lessons.title: Spring Term Number Bonds Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall number bonds to 10 fluently across a range of contexts.
lessons.main_activity: Mixed practice recapping number bonds to 10 using a variety of spring-themed counters (seeds, flowers, eggs).
key_questions: What are all the ways to make 10?
Can you recall this without counting?
lessons.assessment_notes: Assess number bond to 10 fluency progress across the term — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of all bonds to 10.
lessons.home_link: Practise number bonds to 10 with any small objects at home.

lessons.title: Spring Term Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about spring changes and planting learned this half-term.
lessons.main_activity: Contribute to a class 'Spring Changes' display summarising planting, plant parts, and seasonal changes.
key_questions: What have we learned about spring and planting?
What was most interesting?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the half-term's learning — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about spring with your family.

lessons.title: Phonics: Spring 2 Half-Term Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read a range of CVC and digraph words fluently.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all sounds/digraphs learned this half-term.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations consolidating reading across CVC and digraph words in simple sentences.
key_questions: Can you build and read this word?
Can you read this sentence?
lessons.assessment_notes: Update overall phonics tracker with Spring 2 half-term progress.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate progress with a big reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading over the half-term break.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Spring 2 Half-Term Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to demonstrate progress across the half-term's key maths skills.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap key maths learning from across Spring 2.
lessons.main_activity: Rotate through stations reviewing counting, measuring/predicting, symmetry, and number bonds to 10 from across the half-term.
resources_needed: Station resources from across the half-term
key_questions: What have you learned this half-term in maths?
What are you most proud of?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise Spring 2 maths progress overall — evidence for MATHS.1/MATHS.2 across the half-term.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate everyone's maths progress this half-term.
lessons.home_link: Practise favourite maths games together over the half-term break.

lessons.title: Spring 2 Celebration Performance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to perform favourite songs/movements from the half-term with confidence.
lessons.main_activity: Whole-class celebration performance combining favourite songs and movements from the half-term (Easter song, farm song), with plant pots and craft displayed.
key_questions: What was your favourite performance from this half-term?
How did it feel to perform?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe confidence and enjoyment across the half-term's EAD learning — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Round of applause; celebrate a wonderful Spring 2 half-term.
lessons.home_link: Perform a favourite song/dance from this half-term for family over the break.
